page: Amazon Web Services m8g.48xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 192 dedicated physical cores on the ARM64 architecture using the AWS Neoverse-V2 ARMv9 model running at 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a 50 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

In benchmark evaluations, the m8g.48xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance. The stress-ng multi-core test and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression both rank in the top tier. Memory subsystem performance is highly efficient, with read-only small block memory bandwidth reaching 21314.96 GB/sec and large block write bandwidth at 426.41 GB/sec, both placing in the top tier. Database operations and Redis SET operations also achieve top-tier results, with Redis handling 356.88 million operations per second. However, single-core performance remains in the average tier, as shown by stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core metrics.

The instance offers high qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized workloads due to its dedicated physical core allocation with one thread per core and ARM-based architecture, which reduces resource contention compared to hyperthreaded environments. The lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for disk-heavy tasks. The server is highly suited for large-scale multi-threaded applications, software compilation, database hosting, high-throughput static web serving, and medium-model LLM prompt processing.
